dataset: Complete 30-Task Development Benchmark (120 total attempts across High & Low effort)

executive_summary.high_effort: Baseline 12/30 (40.0%) vs Science 11/30 (36.7%) | Discordants: 2 baseline-only (002, 009), 1 science-only (077)
executive_summary.low_effort: Baseline 12/30 (40.0%) vs Science 13/30 (43.3%) | Discordants: 0 baseline-only, 1 science-only (077)
executive_summary.key_thesis: Under lower test-time reasoning tokens, baseline performance stagnates at 12/30 while the science arm improves to 13/30. The code-derived scientific context acts as an external structural memory that replaces internal reasoning loops, recovering tasks (002, 009) that previously failed due to over-deliberation.

transition_tasks.002: High [Base=1, Sci=0] -> Low [Base=1, Sci=1]: Solved by Science under low effort
transition_tasks.009: High [Base=1, Sci=0] -> Low [Base=1, Sci=1]: Solved by Science under low effort
transition_tasks.077: High [Base=0, Sci=1] -> Low [Base=0, Sci=1]: Solved EXCLUSIVELY by Science in BOTH regimes

mechanism_findings.task_077_science_only_win: In both high and low regimes, Science alone solves 077 by immediately locating constructive.py#oriented_envelope via the evidence graph. Baseline searches blind and fails in both regimes.
mechanism_findings.over_deliberation_recovery: In high effort, Science failed 002 and 009 due to lengthy reasoning loops generating complex alternative hypotheses. In low effort, Science directly executes on the graph evidence and succeeds.
mechanism_findings.never_solved_barrier: The 17 never-solved tasks fall into two categories: (1) multi-file architectural bugs exceeding the 24-file scan ceiling (058, 076, 051), and (2) tasks requiring domain-specific numerical solvers that fail regardless of context.
